title: Validator Schema
description: One validator in the central validators/ registry. A validator is a first-class, DEDUPLICATED object: it is defined exactly once and names — via `evidence_sets` — every evidence set it applies to. This mirrors Paramify's own model (the validator owns its evidence-set list), so a validator shared across fetchers is a single file, never a copy. Validators no longer live inline in fetcher.yaml. See docs/validators_design.md.

key.description: Stable repo identity, unique across the registry. Must equal the file's basename (e.g. alb_encryption_in_transit -> validators/aws/alb_encryption_in_transit.yaml). This is what tools reference; it never changes even when `name` does.

type.description: Paramify validator type (REST API v0.8.0). AUTOMATED = a regex over artifact content evaluated by validation_rules. ATTESTATION = reviewer yes/no questions evaluated by attestation_rules (no regex).

role.description: Repo-side classification of what this validator checks (NOT a Paramify field). `completeness` = 'did the collection succeed and is the population real?' — an evidence set has exactly one, and it is where the envelope's exit_code is asserted (see validators/common/collection_succeeded.yaml). `configuration` = a posture check — an evidence set may have many. `integrity` = 'was the field a count-based rule reads actually PRESENT?' — required one-for-one alongside any configuration validator that concludes compliance from a MATCH_COUNT of violations, because zero matches is that validator's pass condition and it therefore cannot distinguish 'no violations' from 'the key I search for is gone'. See docs/validators_design.md.

statement.description: The control statement — what passing this validator asserts (Paramify `statement`).

regex.description: ECMAScript (JavaScript) regex matched against the whole evidence envelope (schema_version + metadata + payload, as written to disk). Its capture groups feed validation_rules. Required for AUTOMATED validators. FLAVOR: Paramify's engine is JavaScript, not Python `re` or PCRE — it applies the `g` and `s` flags automatically but NOT `m`, so `^`/`$` match the whole document and lines are spanned with `[\s\S]*?`. Named groups are `(?<name>…)`; the Python form `(?P<name>…)` is a hard compile error. NAMING: name every capture group, in snake_case derived from the key it captures (`"BackupRetentionPeriod"` -> `backup_retention_period`), unique within the pattern. Naming does not renumber anything — `(?<x>…)` is still group 1 — so validation_rules keeps referencing groups by number. Test with `node`, not Python.

rules_summary.description: Human-readable summary of the pass/fail logic, e.g. 'MATCH_GROUP[1] EQUALS MATCH_GROUP[2]' (Paramify `rules_summary`). Derivable from validation_rules; kept for readability.

validation_rules.description: Structured pass/fail logic for AUTOMATED validators. Rules combine with AND — every rule must hold for the validator to pass (verified on stage 2026-09-03). START EVERY VALIDATOR WITH A PRESENCE RULE: a MATCH_GROUP comparison over a regex that did not match compares nothing to nothing and passes VACUOUSLY, and a MATCH_COUNT-of-violations rule reads a renamed upstream key as zero violations and therefore as compliant. Both are silent false passes. A value-reading validator guards itself with `MATCH_COUNT NOT_EQUALS 0` as its first rule; a violation-counting validator cannot, and needs a separate `role: integrity` validator asserting the structural key exists. Maps to the REST API v0.8.0 `validationRules` (native YAML instead of a JSON string), which documents `regexOperation`/`criteria`/`value` on each rule. The comparison operators are not documented as numeric or lexicographic, so encode numeric thresholds in the regex rather than relying on GREATER_THAN et al.

disposition.description: NOT HONOURED BY THE REST API — verified against a live stage tenant 2026-09-03. POST and PATCH both return HTTP 200 and store the rule with this field removed; three validators differing only in disposition all scored PASS, so it never reaches evaluation, and no alternative key name works. The feature exists in the application UI; the validator endpoints predate it and have not been updated, and a fix is tracked upstream. DO NOT WRITE RULES IN THE NEGATIVE ERROR FORM TODAY: because the field is discarded, every rule becomes a pass-requirement, so the guard pair `MATCH_COUNT EQUALS 0 -> ERROR` plus `exit_code NOT_EQUALS 0 -> ERROR` demands that the envelope be both absent and carrying a non-zero exit code. Measured: a validator written that way is a constant function, returning FAIL on every input including clean evidence. Write collection-health guards POSITIVELY instead (MATCH_COUNT NOT_EQUALS 0, and exit_code EQUALS 0, both plain PASS rules) in a dedicated `role: completeness` validator; when the API starts honouring disposition, migrate by inverting those two rules and adding ERROR here. Semantics when it lands: outcome when this rule's comparison holds. Omitted means PASS (a compliance rule). ERROR means the evidence never arrived, so compliance is UNKNOWN — distinct from FAIL, which means evidence was collected and the control looks bad. See docs/validators_design.md.

regexOperation.description: How the regex result is extracted before comparison.

type.description: MATCH_COUNT = number of matches; MATCH_GROUP = contents of one capture group.

groupNumber.description: Capture group; required when type is MATCH_GROUP.

criteria.description: Comparison operator between the extracted value and `value`.

type.description: MATCH_GROUP uses a capture group (groupNumber); CUSTOM_TEXT uses a literal (customText).

attestation_rules.description: Structured logic for ATTESTATION validators. Maps 1:1 to the REST API v0.8.0 `attestationRules` (native YAML). Empty ([]) for AUTOMATED validators.

question.description: The yes/no question presented to the reviewer.

nestedRules.description: Follow-on rules when a disposition is BASED_ON_NESTED (nestable up to two more layers). Same item shape.

evidence_sets.description: Every evidence set this validator applies to, by stable `reference_id` (matches a fetcher's evidence_set.reference_id). Listing more than one set here IS the dedup mechanism — one validator, many sets, no copies. A reference_id may name a manual/non-automated set that has no fetcher.

allOf.comment: AUTOMATED validators must carry the regex + rules the API's POST /validators requires.
ATTESTATION validators must carry attestation_rules (and no regex logic).
